couplets.label: K1
couplets.question: Underside forewing cell: pair of pale subbasal lines
couplets.a_text: Forewing underside without a pair of pale subbasal lines crossing the discal cell — Pavana group (Four-line Blues)
couplets.b_text: Forewing underside with a pair of pale subbasal lines crossing the discal cell — Berenice / Kurava group (Six-line Blues)
couplets.hint: Hold the forewing to the light and look inside the large closed cell near the wing base. Two pale parallel lines = Six-line Blue (berenice/kurava group). No lines = Four-line Blue (pavana group). This is the primary split for all Nacaduba.

couplets.label: K2
couplets.question: Hindwing underside: prominent rounded black submarginal spot in space 6
couplets.a_text: Hindwing underside with a prominent rounded black submarginal spot in space 6 (near costal margin). FW 14.0–15.5 mm. — Nacaduba angusta
couplets.b_text: Hindwing underside without a prominent submarginal spot in space 6
couplets.hint: In N. angusta the large black spot in HW space 6 is conspicuous and matches a prominent spot in space 2 near the tornus. In all other four-line blues the space-6 spot is absent or very inconspicuous.

couplets.label: K3
couplets.question: Underside postdiscal band: double series of striae with paler space between
couplets.a_text: Postdiscal band composed of a double series of pale striae inwardly bounded by darker lines, with the space between the two striae paler than the ground colour
couplets.b_text: Area between the postdiscal striae unicolorous and of the ground colour (not paler between striae)
couplets.hint: In N. pavana and N. russelli the postdiscal band shows two distinct parallel rows with a noticeably paler gap between them. In N. pactolus, N. hermus, N. subperusia and the larger species the ground colour between the striae is the same as the surrounding wing.

couplets.label: K4
couplets.question: Male upperside wing colour (double-band species, FW 11–12 mm)
couplets.a_text: ♂ upperside pale greyish blue, border a thread; ♀ upperside brown with wedge-shaped pale blue discal patch on FW and basal blue dusting on HW. FW 11.0–12.0 mm. — Nacaduba pavana
couplets.b_text: ♂ upperside rather pale purple blue, border inwardly diffuse; ♀ as in N. pavana but blue patch darker. FW 11.0–12.0 mm. — Nacaduba russelli
couplets.hint: N. pavana males are a distinctive pale greyish-blue. N. russelli males have a richer, more saturated pale purple-blue. Both species are very similar on the underside — male upperside colour is the primary separating character.

couplets.label: K5
couplets.question: Underside striae character: broad and yellowish vs. narrow and well-defined
couplets.a_text: Striae broad, diffuse, and distinctly yellowish; postdiscal band almost blended into ground colour. FW 14.5–16.0 mm. — Nacaduba pactolus
couplets.b_text: Striae narrow and well defined, slightly wider in ♀ than in ♂
couplets.hint: N. pactolus has the broadest, most diffuse, and most yellowish striae in the genus — the postdiscal band almost loses its structure. All other four-line blues in this branch (hermus, subperusia, pendleburyi, solta, sanaya, asaga) have cleaner, narrower, whiter striae.

couplets.label: K6
couplets.question: Hindwing underside: striae in spaces 4 and 5 nearly touching
couplets.a_text: Inner submarginal and outer postdiscal striae in HW spaces 4 and 5 nearly touching (very narrow gap); striae pale buff in ♂, whitish in ♀
couplets.b_text: Inner submarginal and outer postdiscal striae in HW spaces 4 and 5 separated by at least half the width of the postdiscal band
couplets.hint: In N. hermus and N. subperusia the two sets of striae in HW spaces 4–5 are very close and almost touching. In N. pendleburyi, N. solta, N. subperusia intricata, N. sanaya and N. asaga the gap between them is conspicuously wide.

couplets.label: K7
couplets.question: HW tornal spot ring colour and male upperside appearance (spaces 4–5 nearly touching)
couplets.a_text: ♂ upperside violet blue with a slightly frosted appearance (white ribbon scales), border a thread; ♀ upperside pale shining blue with only a very slight purple tinge. HW tornal black spot in space 2 crowned by a brownish-orange ring. FW 13.0–15.0 mm. — Nacaduba hermus
couplets.b_text: ♂ upperside bluish purple, border a thread; ♀ blue areas slightly deeper and more purple than in N. hermus. HW tornal black spot in space 2 crowned by a clear bright orange ring. FW 13.0–15.0 mm. — Nacaduba subperusia lysa
couplets.hint: The ring colour of the HW tornal spot in space 2 is the most reliable character: dull brownish-orange = hermus; clear bright orange = subperusia. The frosted male upperside from white ribbon scales also confirms N. hermus.

couplets.label: K8
couplets.question: Forewing black border widening to at least 1.0 mm at apex (upperside, male)
couplets.a_text: ♂ upperside purplish blue with black border expanding to at least 1.0 mm at FW apex; ♀ upperside paler, less shining blue with rather narrow borders. FW 14.0–16.0 mm. — Nacaduba pendleburyi
couplets.b_text: ♂ upperside forewing black border a thread throughout, not widening at the apex
couplets.hint: Compare the width of the black border at the FW apex vs. along the costa. In N. pendleburyi the border clearly broadens apically. In N. solta, N. subperusia intricata, N. asaga and N. sanaya it remains a narrow thread throughout.

couplets.label: K9
couplets.question: Forewing underside postdiscal band: continuous and almost straight from vein 3 to vein 7
couplets.a_text: FW underside postdiscal band continuous and almost straight from vein 3 to vein 7. ♂ upperside purple with a slight bronzy tint. FW 15.0–16.0 mm. — Nacaduba solta
couplets.b_text: FW underside postdiscal band curved inward toward the base and often slightly dislocated at vein 6
couplets.hint: N. solta has a distinctively straight, unbroken postdiscal band. N. subperusia intricata, N. asaga and N. sanaya all show the band curving inward toward the wing base, with a step or dislocation at vein 6.

couplets.label: K10
couplets.question: Male upperside: veins darker and contrasting; underside striae pale buff
couplets.a_text: ♂ upperside dull purple-blue with veins distinctly darker and contrasting; underside striae pale buff. ♀ upperside more purple than in lysa. FW 15.0–16.0 mm. — Nacaduba subperusia intricata
couplets.b_text: ♂ upperside veins not contrasting; underside striae whitish or white
couplets.hint: N. subperusia intricata is the only species here where the wing veins stand out distinctly darker against a dull purple-blue background, and where the underside striae are pale buff rather than white. N. asaga and N. sanaya have unmarked veins and white striae.

couplets.label: K10b
couplets.question: Male upperside with steely grey tint; or specimen from Borneo
couplets.a_text: ♂ upperside purple with a distinct steely grey tint; ♀ unknown. FW 15.0–16.0 mm. Borneo (Sabah, Sarawak, Brunei). — Nacaduba asaga
couplets.b_text: ♂ upperside shining violet, without steely grey tint; ♀ upperside pale shining silvery blue with a slight greenish tint and broad black borders. FW 13.0–14.5 mm. Malay Peninsula. — Nacaduba sanaya
couplets.hint: N. asaga is restricted to Borneo and has a characteristic steely grey cast on the male upperside; it is also noticeably larger (FW 15–16 mm). N. sanaya occurs on the Malay Peninsula, is smaller (FW 13–14.5 mm), and the male shows a clean shining violet without any grey.

couplets.label: K11
couplets.question: Hindwing underside: two large equal orange-ringed black spots in spaces 1b and 2
couplets.a_text: Two large equal-sized black spots prominently ringed with orange in HW spaces 1b and 2 near the tornus, both conspicuous and visible by transparency on the upperside. — Nacaduba biocellata
couplets.b_text: Tornal markings not as above — no pair of conspicuous, equal orange-ringed black spots in spaces 1b and 2
couplets.hint: The two striking orange-ringed eye-spots of N. biocellata are unique in the genus — both are large, clearly equal in size, and their orange rings show prominently through the wing membrane on the upperside. In all other six-line blues the tornal area is far more subdued.

couplets.label: K12
couplets.question: Underside postdiscal striae: area between striae unicolorous (same as ground colour)
couplets.a_text: Area between the postdiscal striae unicolorous and of the ground colour (striae not inwardly bounded by darker lines). ♂ upperside purple, underside markings not visible by transparency. ♀ FW with a purple-blue patch and bluish spots in spaces 1b and 2. FW 12.0–15.0 mm. — Nacaduba beroe
couplets.b_text: Postdiscal striae inwardly bounded by darker lines, with the space between them paler than the ground colour (character weakly developed in N. kurava ♂)
couplets.hint: In N. beroe the band between the two strial rows blends with the surrounding wing — no distinct paler channel. In N. kurava, N. berenice, N. calauria and N. kirtoni a clearly paler strip runs between the two striae, though it can be subtle in male kurava.

couplets.label: K13
couplets.question: Male upperside: underside markings clearly visible by transparency
couplets.a_text: ♂ upperside violet blue with underside striae clearly visible by transparency through the wing membrane; ♀ upperside pale shining blue turning whitish beyond the FW cell, border rather narrow. FW 13.5–15.0 mm. — Nacaduba kurava
couplets.b_text: ♂ upperside with underside markings barely visible by transparency; ♀ upperside not whitish beyond the FW cell, hindwing mostly brown
couplets.hint: N. kurava has distinctively translucent wings — the underside pattern shows clearly through to the male upperside. N. berenice, N. calauria and N. kirtoni all have more opaque wings where the underside markings do not show through.

couplets.label: K14
couplets.question: Male upperside: pale frosted blue from abundant white ribbon scales
couplets.a_text: ♂ upperside pale frosted blue due to the presence of many white ribbon scales. FW 11.0–13.0 mm. — Nacaduba berenice or N. kirtoni (see K15)
couplets.b_text: ♂ upperside bluish violet, without white ribbon scales; ♀ upperside forewing discal patch darker blue. — Nacaduba calauria
couplets.hint: White ribbon scales give N. berenice (and the very similar N. kirtoni) a pale, frosted or shimmery look in good light. N. calauria males are a deeper, more saturated bluish violet with no frosted appearance. Not applicable to females.

couplets.label: K15
couplets.question: Male upperside tone (ribbon-scale species): pale lavender blue vs slightly more violet
couplets.a_text: ♂ upperside pale lavender blue; ♀ upperside FW with a pale purple-blue patch. FW 11.0–13.0 mm. — Nacaduba berenice
couplets.b_text: ♂ upperside slightly more violet than N. berenice, but barely separable without genitalia examination; ♀ unknown. — Nacaduba kirtoni
couplets.hint: N. berenice and N. kirtoni are essentially indistinguishable in the field — the slight violet tint in male kirtoni is subtle and unreliable. Definitive identification requires examination of male genitalia. Lowland/widespread records default to berenice; highland specimens or genitalia-confirmed records = kirtoni.
